title: Understanding Epistemological Frameworks
text:
Epistemology, a primary branch of philosophy, is fundamentally concerned with the nature, origin, and scope of knowledge. It seeks to answer foundational questions such as: What does it mean to 'know' something? How can we be certain that our beliefs correspond accurately to reality?

The discussion often centers on competing theories regarding how justified true belief (knowledge) is achieved. Rationalism posits that reason and innate ideas are the primary sources of knowledge, suggesting that some truths can be deduced independently of sensory experience. Conversely, empiricism argues strenuously for sensory experience as the sole or principal source of all valid knowledge.

Furthermore, skepticism challenges the very possibility of certain knowledge, questioning whether any claims about reality can ever be definitively proven. These competing frameworks—rationalism, empiricism, and skepticism—form the basis for understanding the limitations and power of human intellect.
